Laravel#

This page wires Rollcall into a Laravel app, and shows the same dashboard as a Vue page in an Inertia app and in a raw PHP app. Next: use it from your coding agent (ADVISOR).

The package registers itself (extra.laravel.providers). Publish the config with php artisan vendor:publish --tag=rollcall-config, set the variables in the configuration reference, and schedule rollcall:scan. The dashboard shows counts and progress; the per-app page is a second route that stays off until you enable it, and it runs behind rollcall.dashboard.internal_middleware (default web and auth.sesame), so an app with no such middleware fails closed. The page uses WayneUI's class names and takes its stylesheet from ROLLCALL_WAYNEUI_CSS. In an Inertia app it can be one of your own Vue pages instead (below). The page also carries a status line (a role="status" paragraph) that names the apps shown and the scan date, so assistive technology hears what the page displays. The /metrics route is registered on its own path; if your app already serves /metrics (HELMET does), run Rollcall's on a separate app or leave metrics off.

The dashboard in an Inertia app (Vue)#

In a Laravel + Inertia + Vue app (WELD's shape) the dashboard can be one of the app's own pages, inside its own layout. Same routes, same switches, same report: with ROLLCALL_DASHBOARD_INERTIA=true the controller hands what DashboardPage::report() built to an Inertia page as props (report, internal, scanCommand) instead of printing the Blade view. From a WELD app:

php artisan vendor:publish --tag=rollcall-inertia   # writes resources/js/pages/Rollcall/Dashboard.vue
# .env: ROLLCALL_DASHBOARD_ENABLED=true and ROLLCALL_DASHBOARD_INERTIA=true
npm run build

The published page is short and it is yours. In essence it puts the component in WELD's AppLayout with a title and a noindex tag:

<script setup lang="ts">
import AppLayout from '@/layouts/AppLayout.vue';
import { Head } from '@inertiajs/vue3';
import RollcallDashboard from '../../../../vendor/waynestate/rollcall/resources/js/RollcallDashboard.vue';

defineProps<{ report: Record<string, unknown> | null; internal: boolean; scanCommand: string }>();
</script>

<template>
    <Head title="Rollcall"><meta name="robots" content="noindex" /></Head>
    <AppLayout>
        <RollcallDashboard :report="report" :internal="internal" :scan-command="scanCommand" />
    </AppLayout>
</template>

Why this shape: the page is published because the layout is the app's, and the component is imported straight from vendor/ because the markup is Rollcall's. composer update moves the component together with the PHP renderer it must match, and there is no npm package to install or keep in step (Rollcall publishes none). Vite and vue-tsc follow the relative import like any file in the project, and the component imports nothing but vue, which the app already has. An app that does not use the Vue page loads none of it; inertiajs/inertia-laravel is needed only when the switch is on.

The component renders what the Blade page shows inside <main>: the same WayneUI classes, the role="status" line, the captions and headers, and the per-app table only on the internal page (<path>/apps, still behind rollcall.dashboard.internal_middleware and ROLLCALL_INTERNAL_ENABLED). It has no style block, no style attribute and no script of its own, so it works under HELMET's CSP, and it takes its look from the app's WayneUI stylesheet. Every Inertia answer carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex. CI holds the rooms together: dashboard-vue server-renders the component with the props the route sends and fails on any difference from the Blade page (elements, attributes and text; only whitespace, attribute order and Vue's hydration comments are normalized), and dashboard-a11y checks the three Vue pages with the other six.

The same page, no framework. rollcall_dashboard() prints the renderer the Laravel page prints, from the same report, so the two answer the roll in the same words. Drop one file into the folder your web server serves:

<?php
// public/rollcall.php
require __DIR__ . '/../vendor/autoload.php';

$helmet = \Waynestate\Helmet\helmet_boot(['preset' => 'citadel']);
rollcall_dashboard(['nonce' => $helmet['nonce']]);

It answers 404 until ROLLCALL_DASHBOARD_ENABLED=true, sends X-Robots-Tag: noindex with every answer, and never runs a scan: it reads the latest snapshot, so set ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE and ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR as for the CLI and schedule vendor/bin/rollcall scan. The page has no script. Its one small style element takes HELMET's nonce; link WayneUI's stylesheet with ROLLCALL_WAYNEUI_CSS and the page keeps its look under HELMET's CSP even without one. No HELMET? Call rollcall_dashboard() with no options. It carries the same status line as the Laravel page.

The per-app page is a second file, behind your sign-in: call rollcall_dashboard(['internal' => true]) after SESAME's sesame_login() has returned a user. It also needs ROLLCALL_INTERNAL_ENABLED=true; with either one missing it answers 404, so it fails closed. For a front controller of your own, Waynestate\Rollcall\Dashboard\RawDashboard::response() returns the same answer as data (status, headers, body).

All three go through the same accessibility gate: DashboardRenderTest writes the Laravel and the raw-PHP pages and the Inertia props, dashboard-vue renders the Vue pages from those props once they match, and dashboard-a11y checks all nine (public, internal and empty, in each room) in light and dark at 320 and 1280 px.
